_meta.principle: Use-case routing hints from anime/illustration A/B testing. These guide model selection for animation/illustration jobs only and must not override brand, product, or text-heavy routing pinned elsewhere.
version_history: 0.1.0 (2026-05-05) — initial 4 locked + 2 split + 3 unsupported from 5-cell test
0.2.0 (2026-05-05) — promoted to 14 locked from v2 15-cell test, demoted manga claim, resolved kids-book split, added text_heavy and lineart locks

character_model_sheet.notes: Locked across both rounds. Multi-view layout, expression strip, equipment callouts, color palette swatches. 12-face expression sheet (cell 03) and 12-pose sheet (cell 10) confirmed NB2 delivers grid count + character consistency where Qwen renders only 7-9 panels with character drift.

expression_sheet_grid.notes: 12-face grid with consistent character identity, labeled emotions, clean grid layout. Qwen produced 9 faces with inconsistent face/hair.

pose_sheet_grid.notes: 12-pose action reference sheet, JP labels, character continuity. Qwen produced 7-8 poses with weaker reference utility.

manga_panel_storytelling.votes: v2: 2/2 (cells 09, 12) — DEMOTED from Qwen claim in v1
manga_panel_storytelling.notes: 4-panel grids with proper gutters, dialogue balloons, sequential beats, and character continuity. Qwen renders 3-panel widescreen strips with character drift. v1 'Qwen wins manga panel composition' claim was style-not-storytelling — DEMOTED.

sequential_4panel_comic.notes: Same as manga_panel_storytelling — gutters + speech balloons + character continuity. NB2's panel-storytelling competence generalizes.

lineart_only_no_atmosphere.notes: Pure black outlines on white, uniform stroke weight, no fills, no shading. Qwen treats 'lineart' as cel-shaded ink with heavy black masses (different aesthetic — fails brief).

watercolor_isolated_sticker.notes: Sticker die-cut white border + white background isolation. Qwen has stronger watercolor texture but renders on solid black — fails the 'isolated' brief.

ghibli_painterly_portrait.notes: 1990s cel-art aesthetic, grain, muted palette, restrained skin texture, atmospheric mood. Council vision_kimi: 'FLUX.2 Pro wins for animation pipeline'.

kids_book_isolated_hero_character.notes: Single hero character on clean background. Better illustrative texture and cleaner anatomy than NB2 for compositing-ready foreground asset.

background_plate_compositing.notes: Cleaner painterly plate with usable depth layers. CAVEAT: both backends produced populated rooms not truly empty plates — re-test with explicit 'no foreground objects, no chairs, no decorations' constraint to lock fully.

prop_orthographic_with_callouts.notes: Industrial-design orthographic with proper dimension lines, leader callouts, named views (front/top/side/back). NB2 character-sheet competence does NOT generalize to engineering-style orthographic — different convention. Lock medium pending second cell.

turnaround_consistency.notes: Front/side/back turnaround with same hair/outfit/proportions across views. NB2 had hair-color drift between front and side views. Counterintuitively NB2 wins expression+pose sheets but LOSES turnaround consistency — different sub-skill.

text_heavy_signage.notes: Multi-line copy (storefront sign 5+ phrases) renders fully legible and correctly spelled. NB2 hallucinated a finance dashboard. CAVEAT: opus_independent_agent flagged this as both_fail — neither backend held the storefront-scene brief; FLUXpro held the text but rendered as UI mockup. For crisp text-on-image, FLUXpro is the lock; for text-INTEGRATED-IN-SCENE, brief still needs work.

flat_vector_editorial_cartoon.notes: Bold outlines, flat fills, expressive faces, integrated street/scene composition with crowd dynamics.

cyberpunk_neon_anime.notes: Atmospheric backlight, neon rim, glowing eyes, layered alley depth. Wins on mood/atmosphere axis.

anime_action_motion_speedlines.notes: Cleaner shonen-anime motion vocabulary. FLUXpro went prop-overload with holographic billboards burying the action. Single-cell evidence — promote to high if next round confirms.

i2v_keyframe_pair_continuity.notes: Pair continuity is the entire point of I2V handoff. Qwen delivered same character + palette + lighting across both start and end frames. FLUXpro broke continuity catastrophically — rendered 3 different characters across the pair. Direct upstream of Veo/Kling I2V pipeline. Most actionable v2 finding.

watercolor_atmospheric_painterly.notes: For mood-piece atmospheric watercolor (no isolation requirement), Qwen leads on texture and brushwork. For isolated-on-white sticker production, route to NB2 (see watercolor_isolated_sticker).

kids_book_full_scenic_spread.council_jury_result: SHIP-WITH-FIXES 2/3 avg 8.0 — did not break tie
kids_book_full_scenic_spread.next_test: Run 4 prompts with explicit constraint: 2 'character must occupy >40% of frame' (NB2 expected) + 2 'rich background storytelling, character secondary' (FLUXpro expected)

demoted_claims.note: Qwen's strength is single-frame anime style fidelity, not comic page composition. NB2 owns panel-storytelling with gutters, balloons, and continuity.

demoted_claims.v2_status: SPLIT-RESOLVED — confirmed for short panel text only
demoted_claims.evidence: v2 cell 12 (dialogue balloons) NB2 wins; v2 cell 13 (storefront signage) NB2 fails, FLUXpro wins
demoted_claims.note: NB2 = good at SHORT readable copy in panel balloons. FLUXpro = better at SUSTAINED multi-word signage. Don't extend NB2 text crown beyond panel use.
v1 single-cell evidence held up in v2.

demoted_claims.evidence: v2 cell 11 — FLUXpro wins, NB2 attempted illustrative grid not engineering orthographic
demoted_claims.note: Character sheets and orthographic prop sheets are different sub-skills. Don't extend NB2 lock to engineering-style technical illustration.

still_unsupported_claims.claim: NB2 has on-image text discipline broadly
still_unsupported_claims.reason: Confirmed for panel balloons only. Storefront/scene signage failed in cell 13.
still_unsupported_claims.next_test: render in-scene billboard with 30+ words at varied sizes
